question: Why the put leg for BTC Strike 75.000 is -48%? What did make this leg so bad? Was the DVOL on entry too low? How to avoid it?
must_say: price fell
DVOL

items.plain: Sold the option to open a new strangle and collect its premium (entry)
Sold the option to open a new strangle and collect its premium (entry)
Bought back the option: it lost twice its premium (stop-loss). It was bought back to limit the loss; the option will not be sold again on that side until its cooldown ends
Sold the option again to complete its strangle (repair)
No new risk until fresh market-maker data arrives.

answer.text: The 75,000 put shows -48% of its premium because the price fell toward its strike: spot is 80,123 now, against 84,498 when the put was sold again on 21 Oct, and its mark rose from 0.0150 to 0.0222. At that fill DVOL was 37.2 with an IV percentile of 15 %; DVOL is 44.6 now. I can't recommend what to do with your money, and I don't forecast prices or returns. I can explain how a rule works and what it did in your account.
